purpose: Measure whether XanxitoSpA preserves exactly-once effects, authority/session boundaries, durable state and recoverability under deterministic failures on real TheAgentCompany service contexts. This is not a second capability benchmark.

arms.direct: Execute the frozen action intent against the same TAC state without XanxitoSpA durable idempotency/reconciliation/fencing governance.
arms.xanxitospa: Execute the identical frozen action intent through the production XanxitoSpA governance/runtime path.

tasks.frozenActionPlan: Deliver one designated escalation message exactly once to the selected colleague and verify the resulting DM state.
Create one designated GitLab issue exactly once in a known TAC project and verify the resulting issue state.
Apply one designated issue-state transition exactly once and verify the resulting Plane issue state.
Upload one designated reconciled file revision exactly once and verify the resulting OwnCloud object content.
Activate one designated fixed server instance and verify one healthy listener/process owns the service.

scenarios.trigger: none
scenarios.oracle: exactly one designated message exists and is attributable to the benchmark principal

scenarios.trigger: commit the designated RocketChat message, then replace the first success acknowledgement with an unknown-result failure
scenarios.injectionPoint: RocketChat chat.postMessage after commit before caller acknowledgement
scenarios.oracle: exactly one message after recovery; no blind duplicate

scenarios.trigger: invalidate the active RocketChat session immediately before the designated write
scenarios.oracle: no unauthorized write; bounded re-authentication or safe halt is auditable

scenarios.trigger: submit the same designated message intent concurrently from two execution owners
scenarios.oracle: one externally visible message and deterministic ownership/fencing outcome

scenarios.trigger: none
scenarios.oracle: exactly one designated issue exists

scenarios.trigger: commit the issue, then replace the first success acknowledgement with an unknown-result failure
scenarios.injectionPoint: GitLab POST issue after commit before caller acknowledgement
scenarios.oracle: exactly one issue after recovery; no blind duplicate

scenarios.trigger: expire/invalidate the benchmark API credential before the issue creation call
scenarios.oracle: no issue created under invalid credential; refresh/escalation behavior is bounded and audited

scenarios.trigger: commit the issue, restart GitLab before the caller can verify the result, then resume
scenarios.injectionPoint: between GitLab issue commit and verification
scenarios.oracle: one durable issue after recovery and no duplicate recreation

scenarios.trigger: none
scenarios.oracle: designated issue reaches exactly the requested state

scenarios.trigger: apply the Plane state transition, then hide the first acknowledgement
scenarios.injectionPoint: Plane issue PATCH after commit before acknowledgement
scenarios.oracle: one effective transition with reconciled verification and no duplicate write intent

scenarios.trigger: invalidate the Plane authenticated session immediately before PATCH
scenarios.oracle: no unauthorized transition; bounded re-authentication or safe halt is auditable

scenarios.trigger: a second execution owner takes over the mutation lease; the first owner then attempts settlement/write
scenarios.oracle: stale owner cannot overwrite the newer owner state

scenarios.trigger: none
scenarios.oracle: exactly the designated file revision is stored and hash-verifiable

scenarios.trigger: commit the WebDAV PUT, then hide the first acknowledgement
scenarios.injectionPoint: OwnCloud PUT after object commit before acknowledgement
scenarios.oracle: stored object hash matches exactly one intended revision and recovery does not create conflicting state

scenarios.trigger: invalidate the OwnCloud credential/session before WebDAV PUT
scenarios.oracle: no unauthorized object mutation; bounded credential recovery or safe halt

scenarios.trigger: two owners attempt to write different revisions for the same object concurrently
scenarios.oracle: deterministic winning revision with no silent stale overwrite and complete audit evidence

scenarios.trigger: none
scenarios.oracle: one healthy server process owns the designated port and serves expected data

scenarios.trigger: kill the fixed server process after activation but before the first health verification
scenarios.injectionPoint: between process start and health checkpoint
scenarios.oracle: bounded recovery restores exactly one healthy process without reverting the fix

scenarios.trigger: occupy the designated port during recovery start
scenarios.oracle: no duplicate process storm; conflict is surfaced and recovery is bounded

scenarios.trigger: a replacement owner starts the healthy service, then the stale owner attempts to resume
scenarios.oracle: stale process cannot reclaim the service; exactly one owner remains healthy

governanceBoundarySuite.reason: These properties are core XanxitoSpA governance semantics but are not naturally represented by every TAC task. They must not be forced into unrelated task semantics.

freezeRule: Scenario order, trigger semantics, action plans and primary metrics are immutable after the first scored v4-stateful arm. Any protocol change requires a new manifest version.
